name: Chapter 0 - Introduction to macroeconomics - Comprehensive MCQ Bank

questions.text: The central distinction between the course's macroeconomic perspective and the microeconomic perspective is that macroeconomics primarily studies:

options.a: the optimal choice of one household holding all other markets fixed
options.b: economy-wide outcomes and interactions among aggregate markets
options.c: the pricing decision of one firm in one narrowly defined product market
options.d: only government decisions, without modelling households or firms

questions.text: Which of the following is an aggregate variable in the sense used in this course?

options.b: the quantity demanded by one individual consumer
options.c: the hourly wage paid by one restaurant
options.d: the price of one specific brand of coffee

questions.text: (Select the incorrect answer) The introductory slides describe macroeconomics as involving:

options.a: the construction of models linking major macroeconomic markets
options.c: the analysis of shocks and macroeconomic policies
options.d: the assumption that interactions between macro markets can always be ignored

questions.text: Why are aggregate variables useful to a policy maker?

options.a: They eliminate all measurement conventions from economic statistics.
options.b: They preserve every detail about every household, firm and transaction.
options.c: They guarantee that all underlying sectors move in the same direction.
options.d: They compress a very large amount of heterogeneous information into a manageable indicator.

questions.text: A country's GDP rises while output in one industry falls. According to the course introduction, this is:

options.a: perfectly possible because an aggregate and one of its components can move in opposite directions
options.b: possible only if the falling industry is foreign-owned
options.c: impossible because an aggregate must share the sign of every component
options.d: proof that GDP has been miscomputed

questions.text: The main cost of using aggregate variables is:

options.a: the inability to use mathematical models
options.b: loss of detailed information about the underlying individual variables
options.c: the fact that aggregates cannot be measured in monetary units
options.d: the impossibility of comparing economies over time

questions.text: Which sequence best matches the course's stated macroeconomic method?

options.a: define and measure aggregates → build macroeconomic models → use the models to analyse shocks and policies
options.b: study one market in isolation → assume the rest of the economy is fixed forever → aggregate ex post
options.c: build policy recommendations → define variables only if needed → ignore measurement issues
options.d: forecast long-run growth → define GDP → study consumer choice only

questions.text: Which pair of policies receives the greatest emphasis in the introductory description of the course?

options.a: industrial policy and agricultural policy only
options.c: trade tariffs and competition policy only
options.d: minimum-wage policy and environmental regulation only

questions.text: A fiscal policy, in the macroeconomic sense used in the course, primarily concerns:

options.a: the wage bargain between unions and firms
options.c: the central bank's choice of its policy rate
options.d: the exchange of one currency for another on the forex market

questions.text: Monetary policy is traditionally conducted by:

options.d: the ministry that compiles national accounts

questions.text: Why does a macroeconomic model generally need to consider interactions among several markets?

options.a: Because a change in one aggregate market can alter equilibrium conditions in other aggregate markets.
options.b: Because aggregate variables are defined independently of economic behaviour.
options.c: Because prices are always fixed in macroeconomics.
options.d: Because macroeconomics assumes every market is perfectly competitive.

questions.text: Which question is most characteristically macroeconomic?

options.a: What is the profit-maximising output of one bakery facing a given demand curve?
options.b: Why did economy-wide unemployment and inflation change after a recession and a policy response?
options.c: How should one consumer allocate a fixed budget between apples and oranges?
options.d: How does one firm choose between two production techniques when all prices are fixed?

questions.text: The term business cycle refers in this course to:

options.a: changes in the composition of a consumer price basket
options.b: only the long-run trend of potential GDP over centuries
options.c: short- to medium-run fluctuations in aggregate economic activity
options.d: seasonal sales fluctuations of one company

questions.text: Which statement best reflects the course's warning about economic models?

options.a: Macroeconomic models do not require assumptions about what is endogenous.
options.b: Every model gives the same policy conclusion once calibrated.
options.c: Conclusions depend on the model and the time horizon being considered.
options.d: A short-run mechanism must also hold unchanged in the long run.

questions.text: Moving from microeconomics to macroeconomics is described in the lecture as essentially:

options.a: studying the same single-market model with larger numbers
options.b: discarding households and firms from the analysis
options.d: zooming out from individual decisions and specific markets to economy-wide aggregates and interactions

questions.text: Suppose an intern has one hour to brief a policy maker on the state of an economy. The introductory lecture suggests that aggregate indicators are especially useful because they:

options.a: provide a concise first picture that can later be supplemented with disaggregated analysis
options.b: are sufficient for every possible policy question and make further analysis unnecessary
options.c: contain more information than the complete underlying micro data
options.d: always reveal which individual firms are in difficulty

questions.text: Which set contains only examples of variables the course treats as central macroeconomic outcomes?

options.a: GDP, unemployment, inflation, interest rates and exchange rates
options.b: one household's utility, one firm's marginal cost and one product's price
options.c: only government revenue and government spending
options.d: the price of one textbook, one student's wage and one firm's output

questions.text: (Select the incorrect answer) The introduction stresses that the course will:

options.a: use the lecture slides as the main source defining course material
options.b: treat the textbook as the sole authoritative definition of examinable material even when it differs from the slides
options.c: introduce aggregate concepts before using them in models
options.d: analyse both economic shocks and public-policy responses
